Thicker scintillator crystals are embedded in a tungsten, rather than stainless steel, grid. This thicker, high-Z material increases the chance of interaction between the x-rays that pass through the experimental target and strike the scintillator, yielding an increase in the capture of useful radiographic image data (i.e., quanta). This improved DQE provides higher image quality, enabling imaging of submillimeter features within a thicker object. The photos of J. Robert Oppenheimer visually convey the concept of DQE. A higher DQE (top right), in which more quanta are captured, yields more informa- tion to create an image, whereas a lower DQE (bottom right) captures less information and thus yields a lower quality image.
